questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location, english speaking country. And some where not to far from home.

Additional comments:

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction to the campus and finding out which courses to take.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The welcome week is pretty overwhelming but there is a lots of different things you can participate in which is super nice.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed with a private student accommodation but got i through the university

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a good idea to live with other students, especially with other students who also doing there exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to apply with some basic information and then a personal statement. And then you also had to look a possible courses to take at the university. All in all not that complicated a process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to the students advisors and you also got an academic co-hort.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses i wanted more or less.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: depending on what school you are visiting they are very happy to help, the level on introduction help depends on the school

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the set up for the chemistry quite different, so the opportunity the take more selective courses are not that good. Therefore there were a lot that was very wellknown and some topic i didn't know anything about. I took 3 year courses, but would possibly look into takeing 4 year course in something you are familiar with.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style is very much alike, but the the chemistry courses consist of 5 courses per course, And you don't really know what they are about beforehand / have the opportunity the study the topics you find relevant.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Chemistry 3A
Chemistry 3B
History of medicine

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Not really, but would recommend to take a course in something completely different then what you are used to. You just have to pass so it is a good opportunity to explore something else, without the pressure of having to do well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: cheap coffee, and the pubs.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to bring ID when you are going out. 
Go to different resturants there are a lot of good places top eat and it is cheaper then Copenhagen.
go to the pub quiz at Southsider, remember to study Scottish geography and sports names before.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Scotland is not England, and they are scottish not british
